items.followUp: Define intermolecular forces and explain how hydrogen bonding occurs between water molecules.

rubric.description: Defines intermolecular forces as attractions between molecules.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the forces as attractions acting between molecules, rather than within a molecule's bonds.

rubric.why: States which atoms commonly give rise to hydrogen bonding.
rubric.description: Identifies hydrogen bonded to F, O, or N as a condition for hydrogen bonding.
rubric.how: Award for naming hydrogen bonded to at least one of fluorine, oxygen, or nitrogen.

rubric.why: Explains the attraction responsible for hydrogen bonding.
rubric.description: Explains that the hydrogen is attracted to a lone pair on an electronegative atom of a neighboring molecule.
rubric.how: Award for linking hydrogen to a lone pair on another molecule.

rubric.why: Gives a relevant example of hydrogen bonding.
rubric.description: Gives water molecules as an example of hydrogen bonding.
rubric.how: Award for identifying hydrogen bonding between water molecules.

rubric.why: Adds a consequence that demonstrates the strength of hydrogen bonding.
rubric.description: States that hydrogen bonding raises a substance's boiling point or otherwise affects its physical properties.
rubric.how: Award for a correct property effect attributed to hydrogen bonding.

modelAnswer: Intermolecular forces are attractive forces that act between molecules and are generally weaker than the bonds within molecules.
Hydrogen bonding is a strong intermolecular attraction that occurs when hydrogen is bonded to a highly electronegative atom, usually F, O, or N.
The partially positive hydrogen of one molecule is attracted to a lone pair on an F, O, or N atom of a neighboring molecule.
For example, hydrogen bonds form between water molecules.
Hydrogen bonding raises boiling points and affects other physical properties.

items.followUp: Give two uses of inorganic chemistry in industry or daily life.

rubric.why: Provides one valid application of inorganic chemistry.
rubric.description: Names the manufacture or use of fertilizers as an application.
rubric.how: Award for a relevant application involving fertilizers.

rubric.description: Names another valid application, such as producing cement, glass, metals, ceramics, or pesticides.
rubric.how: Award for a valid application different from the first.

modelAnswer: Inorganic chemistry is applied in the manufacture of fertilizers.
It is also applied in producing materials such as cement, glass, and metals.

items.followUp: Differentiate between an element and a compound.

rubric.why: States the defining composition of a homogeneous mixture.
rubric.description: A homogeneous mixture has a uniform composition throughout.
rubric.how: Award for stating that its composition is uniform or the same throughout.

rubric.why: States the defining composition of a heterogeneous mixture.
rubric.description: A heterogeneous mixture has a non-uniform composition, with distinguishable parts or phases.
rubric.how: Award for stating that it is non-uniform or that its components/phases can be distinguished.

modelAnswer: A homogeneous mixture has a uniform composition throughout, and its components are not visibly distinguishable.
A heterogeneous mixture has a non-uniform composition, and its components or phases can be distinguished.

items.followUp: Define a molecule and molecular mass.

rubric.why: Defines a formula unit in terms of the ions in an ionic compound.
rubric.description: A formula unit is the simplest whole-number ratio of ions represented in an ionic compound's formula.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the simplest whole-number ratio of ions.

rubric.why: Defines formula mass as a sum of atomic masses.
rubric.description: Formula mass is the sum of the atomic masses of all atoms represented in a formula unit.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the atomic masses of the formula's atoms are added.

modelAnswer: A formula unit is the simplest whole-number ratio of positive and negative ions in an ionic compound.
Formula mass is the sum of the atomic masses of all atoms represented in the formula unit.

items.followUp: Define atomic radius and state the atomic radius of oxygen.

rubric.why: Gives an accepted definition of atomic radius.
rubric.description: Defines atomic radius as half the distance between the nuclei of two identical bonded atoms, or as the distance from the nucleus to the outermost shell.

rubric.why: Gives the accepted carbon atomic-radius value.
rubric.description: States the atomic radius of carbon as 0.077 nm (77 pm).
rubric.how: Award for the correct value in an equivalent unit.

modelAnswer: Atomic radius is half the distance between the nuclei of two identical atoms bonded together.
The atomic radius of carbon is 0.077 nm (77 pm).

items.followUp: State two features of the long-form periodic table.

rubric.why: States the basis on which elements are arranged.
rubric.description: Elements in the long-form periodic table are arranged in increasing atomic number.
rubric.how: Award for stating that atomic number increases across the arrangement.

rubric.description: Identifies a correct feature such as its seven periods, eighteen groups, period number indicating shells, or similar valence-electron configurations within a group.
rubric.how: Award for one correct structural or group/period feature.

modelAnswer: In the long-form periodic table, elements are arranged in order of increasing atomic number.
It has seven periods and eighteen groups; the period number indicates the number of electron shells.

items.followUp: What is the difference between a bonding pair and a non-bonding pair of electrons?

rubric.why: Describes a lone pair as not participating in a bond.
rubric.description: A lone pair is a pair of valence electrons belonging to one atom and not shared in a bond.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the pair is unshared or belongs to one atom.

rubric.why: Describes a bond pair as shared between atoms.
rubric.description: A bond pair is a pair of electrons shared by two atoms in a covalent bond.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the pair is shared between atoms.

modelAnswer: A lone pair is a pair of valence electrons that is not shared in bonding and belongs to one atom.
A bond pair is a pair of electrons shared between two atoms to form a covalent bond.

items.followUp: Describe the covalent bond between the two nitrogen atoms in an N₂ molecule.

rubric.why: Identifies the bond order in nitrogen molecules.
rubric.description: States that the nitrogen atoms form a triple covalent bond by sharing three pairs of electrons.
rubric.how: Award for identifying a triple covalent bond or three shared pairs.

rubric.why: Describes the components of the triple bond.
rubric.description: States that the triple bond consists of one sigma bond and two pi bonds.
rubric.how: Award for correctly identifying one sigma and two pi bonds.

modelAnswer: In an N₂ molecule, the nitrogen atoms share three pairs of electrons, forming a triple covalent bond (N≡N).
This triple bond consists of one sigma bond and two pi bonds.
